status.en: 22 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Addis Ababa.
status.nb: 22 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Addis Ababa.

summary.en: Ethiopian forces have installed an interim government in Tigray and are moving toward the Eritrean border, while a pro-government militia says it has seized the regional airport. The militia also reports that Eritrean forces have suffered losses in the fighting. The United States, through Secretary of State Marco Rubio, is urging Ethiopia and Eritrea to de-escalate the conflict. Hospitals in Tigray have resumed operations as supplies arrive, and the conflict caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Etiopiske styrker har installert en midlertidig regjering i Tigray og beveger seg mot den eritreiske grensen, mens en pro-regjeringsmilits sier den har tatt kontroll over den regionale flyplassen. Militsen rapporterer også at eritreiske styrker har lidd tap i kampene. USA, gjennom utenriksminister Marco Rubio, oppfordrer Etiopia og Eritrea til å dempe konflikten. Sykehus i Tigray har gjenopptatt driften etter at forsyninger har ankommet, og konflikten forårsaket 2 824 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
